# Nvidia quarterly sales are expected to nearly double to about $109 billion

Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday after the close, with Wall Street looking for sales just above the company's $108 billion outlook.

By Opening Bell Daily Staff

Nov 13, 2026

Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday after the close, with Wall Street looking for about $109 billion in quarterly sales. [...] That would be nearly double the $57.0 billion the company recorded a year earlier, and up 13% from the $96.2 billion it posted in the July quarter.

The estimate sits just above the $108 billion midpoint Nvidia guided to in August, and inside its plus or minus 2% range. Analysts also look for adjusted earnings of about $2.48 a share, up from $2.22 last quarter and well above the $1.30 Nvidia earned a year ago. [...] Tuesday's report is the first real check on whether demand is still strong enough to meet that outlook.

results.title: Nvidia announces Vera Rubin racks that can be shipped on a truck
results.content:
In this article

Nvidia announced Wednesday a new product that will put seven of its Vera Rubin AI racks into a shipping container, the company's latest effort to move up the stack and offer complete systems for artificial intelligence computing. [...] The DSX Pod is a reference design that will ship from Nvidia's manufacturing partners. Nvidia said it was working with manufacturers including Foxconn, Gigabyte, Lenovo, HPE, Quanta and Pegatron. Nvidia expects deliveries to start in early 2027. [...] The DSX Pod AI factory will reduce the time for a new AI data center to start serving tokens from six months to 14 days, according to the company. Nvidia said the pod is intended for customers worldwide and could help address deployment challenges faced by European customers.

Nvidia did not announce a price for the system, but analysts say a single Vera Rubin rack can cost more than $7 million.

## Recent developments
* **CEO Transition & Investigation:** On November 12, 2026, Jensen Huang resigned as CEO following revelations that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort and engaged in relationships with individuals tied to Chinese business/intelligence circles [1, 2, 4, 5]. Colette Kress, EVP and CFO, was appointed interim CEO, and Harvey C. Jones was named the first-ever Chair of the Board [1, 5]. An independent board investigation is ongoing [3].
* **Financial Performance:** Wall Street estimates point to record quarterly sales nearing $109 billion (nearly double year-over-year) and adjusted EPS around $2.47–$2.48, ahead of NVIDIA's upcoming earnings report [7, 8, 9]. 
* **Product & Infrastructure Announcements:** NVIDIA recently unveiled DSX POD AI factories to accelerate European and global infrastructure deployment, alongside Vera Rubin racks designed for rapid containerized shipping [10, 11]. NVIDIA also announced partnerships with Nokia and telecom operators to transform networks into distributed intelligence platforms [12], as well as a collaboration with Rebellions and SK Telecom for sovereign AI infrastructure using NVLink Fusion [1].
* **Supply Chain Expansion:** In late October 2026, NVIDIA announced major supply chain capacity agreements, including a $1.1 billion capacity reservation advance to KYEC to support new U.S., Taiwanese, and Singaporean semiconductor testing facilities [13].

## Talking points
* **Interim Leadership and Stability:** Address the transition strategy under Interim CEO Colette Kress and assure stakeholders of operational continuity during the executive search [1].
* **Growth and Q3 Earnings Outlook:** Review the expected doubling of quarterly revenue to ~$109 billion and evaluate whether demand signals remain strong enough to maintain momentum [7].
* **Sovereign AI and Product Rollouts:** Discuss the commercial timeline for Vera Rubin racks, DSX POD AI factories, and the recent telecom/sovereign AI infrastructure partnerships with Nokia, SK Telecom, and Rebellions [1, 10, 11, 12].
* **Supply Chain Resilience:** Highlight ongoing capacity expansions—such as the $1.1 billion testing agreement with KYEC across the U.S., Singapore, and Taiwan—aimed at supporting volume growth heading into 2027 [13].

## Open questions
* Who is being considered for the permanent CEO role, and what is the expected timeline for the appointment?
* What are the preliminary findings or compliance implications of the ongoing independent board investigation regarding the former CEO?
* How will the executive leadership transition impact upcoming enterprise delivery timelines for Vera Rubin systems and DSX POD AI factories?
